question:
A 44-year-old woman presents with increased thirst and frequent urination that started 6 months ago and have progressively worsened. Recently, she also notes occasional edema of the face. She has no significant past medical history or current medications. The patient is afebrile and the rest of the vital signs include: blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg, heart rate is 61/min, respiratory rate is 14/min, and temperature is 36.6°C (97.8°F). The BMI is 35.2 kg/m2. On physical exam, there is 2+ pitting edema of the lower extremities and 1+ edema in the face. There is generalized increased deposition of adipose tissue present that is worse in the posterior neck, upper back, and shoulders. There is hyperpigmentation of the axilla and inguinal areas. The laboratory tests show the following findings:
Blood
Erythrocyte count 4.1 million/mm3
Hgb 12.9 mg/dL
Leukocyte count 7,200/mm3
Platelet count 167,000/mm3
Fasting blood glucose 141 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L)
Creatinine 1.23 mg/dL (108.7 µmol/L)
Urea nitrogen 19 mg/dL (6.78 mmol/L)
Urine dipstick
Glucose +++
Protein ++
Bacteria Negative
The 24-hour urine protein is 0.36 g. Which of the following medications is the best treatment for this patient’s condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fasting blood glucose 141 mg/dL" -> "Glucose +++ in urine dipstick" -> "Likely diabetes mellitus" -> 80% CHAIN: "Likely diabetes mellitus" -> "Hyperglycemia" -> "Increased osmotic diuresis" -> 70% CHAIN: "Increased osmotic diuresis" -> "Polyuria" -> "Dehydration" -> 60% CHAIN: "Dehydration" -> "Increased thirst" -> "Frequent urination" -> 50% CHAIN: "Likely diabetes mellitus" -> "Insulin deficiency or resistance" -> "Hyperglycemia" -> 70% CHAIN: "Insulin deficiency or resistance" -> "Impaired glucose uptake by cells" -> "Hyperglycemia" -> 70% CHAIN: "Hyperglycemia" -> "Polyuria" -> "Dehydration" -> 60% CHAIN: "Dehydration" -> "Increased thirst" -> "Frequent urination" -> 50% CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "Decreased blood glucose levels" -> "Improved symptoms of diabetes mellitus" -> 80%
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms and signs consistent with Cushing's syndrome, likely due to an adrenal tumor secreting excess cortisol. The presence of hyperglycemia, proteinuria, and edema further supports this diagnosis. The best treatment option for this patient's condition would be metoprolol, a beta-blocker that can help manage some of the cardiovascular manifestations of Cushing's syndrome.
